title: Welcome to ST201
text:
Welcome to second year and welcome to ST201!
We will be covering lots of things data related. This will range from the different types of data, how to summarise and visualise data, perform hypothesis tests, and interpret simple linear regression models


On successful completion of the module, you should be able to

Calculate probabilities in R.
Analyse one and two samples using standard parametric methods.
Display data using graphical methods.
Fit, interpret and predict from simple linear regression models.




This module is 100% continuous assessment which is broken down into three parts

4 assignments in the form of a Moodle quiz (worth 15%)
1 mid-term exam, which will be held on November 10th @3pm (worth 10%)
1 final exam, which will be held on January 7th @10am (worth 75%)







ImportantDetails for Erasmus students



If you are an Erasmus student here for Semester 1 only (September - December), you will not be here for the final exam. With that in mind, your assignments and mid-term will be worth more marks.
If you are here for the full academic year (semester 1 AND semester 2), then your grades will follow the same breakdown as listed above.

title: Welcome to ST201
text:
Slides
All the slides for this module are created using Quarto. In fact, this entire module website is built using Quarto. Personally, I love Quarto. I do just about everything with it! If you every get a chance, do check it out (ok … mini rant over!)

There are many little hidden things you can do with these slides.
You can click in the slides and navigate through them with ← and →.
If you type ? (or shift + /) while viewing the slides you can see a list of slide-specific commands (such as like f for fullscreen mode or additionally s for presenter mode if you want to see my notes).
Finally, if you want to make a PDF of these slides you can press e, followed by ctrl + p.

title: Lecture overview
text:
Each class has a set of required readings that should be completed in your own time. For the most part, these readings will mirror what we have covered in the lectures. However, there will be times that I find a cool resource that I believe may be helpful for some of you.
All the slides for this module are special HTML files made using both Quarto and Clean Revealjs theme by Grant McDermott. Personally, this is my favourite theme to use for presentations, although I have made a couple of minor tweaks to it myself
